identification: Octagonal blue and white meat platter, pagoda/bridge/figures landscape in trellis and cartouche border, probably Chinese export porcelain (Qianlong, late 18th c.). Unmarked, orange-pink coating under the well, rim frits and chips likely. Could also be a later copy.

viewing_check: Handle it. Is the body hard-paste porcelain (glassy, bluish glaze, no crazing; unglazed foot rim, any spur or sand marks) or soft English earthenware/transfer print (painted brushwork vs printed dots, visible under loupe)? Photograph the underside close up and the foot rim and the orange-pink coating (possible Chinese iron-red or bole wash, or later residue), and measure length. Check each rim chip, hairlines and any restoration by UV or a light behind.
rate_note: All prices AUD as printed; no currency conversion used.
